messages:
maya: hey team, noticing negative values and large gaps in the 'tokens/sec' streaming panel for customer acct=redwood-qa. started ~ 11:12 UTC, visible across two consecutive 1m windows. screenshot pasted :point_up:

samir: can you attach the query + time range you used? also which model route / prod vs staging?

maya: prod, route=model-gen-v2, dashboard time range 11:10-11:20 UTC. query is the standard streaming_tokens_per_sec aggregation on 1m windows. grabbing logs now.

maya: logs (filtered by route):
```
2026-03-04T11:11:00Z INFO metrics/ingest: route=model-gen-v2 window=2026-03-04T11:11:00Z tokens=3245
2026-03-04T11:12:00Z INFO metrics/ingest: route=model-gen-v2 window=2026-03-04T11:12:00Z tokens=-128
2026-03-04T11:13:00Z INFO metrics/ingest: route=model-gen-v2 window=2026-03-04T11:13:00Z tokens=0
```

anne: :eyes: negative token counts in ingest logs. that's a red flag — either an upstream meter emitted a delta with wrong ordering or our aggregator did a subtraction in the wrong order. any recent deploys to metrics-aggregator?

diego: I rolled a small change to the aggregator last night (timestamp alignment fix). I only touched out-of-order handling, but didn't expect sign flips. looking.

samir: quick repro checklist: 1) confirm order of event timestamps, 2) check for duplicate sequence IDs, 3) run aggregation locally with the same windowing code. maya can you share the raw events for those windows?

maya: raw events (sanitized):
```
{ts:1614949860000, seq: 9872, tokens: 3245}
{ts:1614949920000, seq: 9873, tokens: -137}
{ts:1614949980000, seq: 9874, tokens: 1450}
```
note the negative tokens value is present in the second event, so the upstream meter definitely emitted a negative delta for that run.

ops-bot: alert: customer-redwood-qa streaming_tokens_per_sec anomaly detected (rule: negative-value). ticket created: SPT-4129

anne: thanks. open a support ticket for the customer and mark as P2 escalation. also capture correlation_id from API logs for affected requests.

maya: filed internal support ticket SPT-4129, added correlation ids. customer-facing note: "we see intermittent negative token counts in analytics. investigating ingest pipeline; no user access impact."

diego: I pulled the deploy diff — I added an optimization that computes delta = next.tokens - prev.tokens but I had an accidental cast to signed 32-bit when events are unsigned 64. overflow could produce negative numbers for specific sequences.

samir: that explains it. can you revert the optimized build and roll a patch to clamp deltas so negative token deltas are treated as 0 unless explicitly flagged by upstream? we should also add a short-term dashboard clamp to avoid negative plotting.

diego: creating rollback PR now. patch will: 1) clamp negative deltas to 0 at aggregator output, 2) add a guard for overflow by using unsigned math, 3) add unit test. will deploy to staging, then canary to prod.

maya: for remediation I manually patched the dashboard query to `GREATEST(tokens_per_sec, 0)` to avoid showing negatives for customers. updated dashboard and alerted customer.

anne: good mitigation. please add postmortem notes to SPT-4129 with root cause (signed cast overflow) and timeline. also add a regression test that replays large seq numbers.

samir: follow-up: add an alert that triggers when any tokens/sec < 0 in production for >1 minute (auto-create ticket). previously we only alerted on zeros.

diego: rollback PR: https://git.internal/redwood/metrics-aggregator/pulls/482 — running canary now (canary group=10% traffic).

maya: can you also confirm if this affected billing/usage pipeline? customer says billing looked normal but wants reassurance.

diego: billing ingestion reads raw tokens from the metering service (downstream of collector) and uses monotonic counters, not the aggregated deltas. I don't see negative numbers in the billing pipeline. double-checking raw meter stream now.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary deployment started for pr-482 on metrics-aggregator (canary=10%).

maya: customer updated: "thanks for the quick response — we've seen the dashboard fix and no bill impact so far." :relieved: 

anne: next steps: 1) confirm canary healthy for 30m, 2) promote rollback, 3) patch dashboard to clamp until next release, 4) add unit + replay tests to prevent regression. assigning owners in SPT-4129.

samir: closing loop — thanks everyone. great catch. :tada:
